title: The Crossing
voice: Plain statement, one image to a line, feeling held back: the song as Pound made Cathay out of another man's word-by-word notes.

lines.en: Between the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā a boat goes.
The Mātaṅgī girl has plunged in. She ferries across, playing.
Row, Ḍombī. Row, Ḍombī. The way is open.
By the true guru's feet I will go again to the Jina's city.
Five oars fall at the prow. The rope is tied at the stern.
Bail with the sky-scoop. The water does not come in at the seams.
Moon and sun: two wheels. Creation and destruction: the pulinda.
Two roads, left and right. Look at neither. Row as you please.
She takes no cowrie, she takes no coin. She ferries across of her own accord.
Those who climbed into a chariot cannot row. They sink, shore after shore.

couplets.kept: Each image closed in its own sentence, so the rivers, the boat and the plunging girl arrive one at a time.
couplets.letGo: The beat of the source's half-line.

couplets.kept: The call repeated whole; the refrain comes back word for word, the one hot thing in a cool version.
couplets.letGo: The off rhyme uchārā / jiṇaurā, and any steady beat.

couplets.kept: The boat's gear named plainly, the sky-scoop left as strange as it is.
couplets.letGo: The perfect rhyme of bāndhī / sāndhi.

couplets.kept: The riddle set out as bare equations, moon and sun: two wheels, with no answer.
couplets.letGo: The off rhyme of pulindā / chandā.

couplets.kept: The doubled refusal of payment, and the flat last sentence of the sinking.
couplets.letGo: Nothing the source has here, except its music.

note: An example made with Claude: the cool pole of the Workshop board, to hear what the images do alone. Set it beside 'Row, Ḍombī'.
